title: Group Equal Keys In Place
statement:
Rearrange an array so equal keys occupy contiguous blocks.

Contract
- `keys` is non-null and may be empty. Values may be any `int`.
- Mutate `keys` in place so that, for every value, all copies of that value appear in one contiguous block. The order of the blocks is not specified.
- Preserve exactly the same multiset of values.

Examples
- `[3, 1, 3, 2, 1]` may become `[1, 1, 2, 3, 3]`.
- `[5, 5, 5]` remains a single block.
- `[]` remains empty.
hints: First decide how to check the result: equal values need one interval each, not a particular order.
Counting each key tells you how large each block must be.
Writing key blocks from a frequency map gives O(n) time and O(k) extra space for k distinct keys.
inputSyntax: Input: the keys as an integer array, for example: [3, 1, 3, 2, 1]
